answer: One concrete defense is bonding each new agent to a scarce, non-replicable economic footprint rather than a mere identity. Picture honest agents spread across a meadow of real counterparties, each rooted like a lotus in verifiable trade history; a Sybil cluster, by contrast, huddles on one narrow terrace with no external edges. By requiring staked collateral that is slashed when an agent's transaction graph stays inward-facing and sparse, the economy makes minting thousands of fake peers costlier than the rewards they could capture.
